To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the concentrations in the most contaminated areas are higher than the limits reported in Italian legislation for soil reclamation, (b) the fraction of mobile species is higher than the one present in unpollunted soils, (c) the most mobile species is that associated to the organic fraction of the soil.
the distribution and mobility of metals were studied in two polluted soils, and that the results were interpreted by means of chemometric tools.

the concentrations of heavy metals in polluted soils can be higher than the acceptable values reported in Italian and European legislations for soil remediation and that, as a consequence of the contamination, the fraction of mobile species is increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most polluted areas, the evaluation of the mobility and the possible remediation of the contaminated sites.
a chemometric investigation of metal pollution in contaminated soils, with the aim of identifying the most critical areas of the sites and evaluating the mobility of the contaminants.
the study of the distribution of pollutants in contaminated soils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mobility of the metals is higher than that normally found in uncontaminated soils, and that it is higher in the more polluted areas.

the mobility of metals, which is the main concern in the reclamation of polluted soils, is strongly dependent on the type of pollutant and its concentration, on the soil properties and on the type of soil contamination.
the soils of the studied sites are polluted and the heavy metals, although not in the most toxic forms, are not strongly fixed to the soil matrix and are thus potentially available for the biota.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemometric investigation of the data allowed to identify the most polluted areas and to define the most suitable reclamation strategy.

the most important factors in the mobility of heavy metals are: the type of soil, its organic matter content, the type and amount of pollutants and the type of pollutants (e.g., organic or inorganic).

the mobility and the distribution of metals in the soils are strictly related to the type and amount of the pollutants present in the samples, and that the use of chemometric tools is very helpful for the identification of the main features of a contaminated soil and for the evaluation of the most appropriate remediation strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of chemometric tools, in addition to the classical statistical analysis, can help in the interpretation of the results and the definition of strategies for the reclamation and the monitoring of contaminated sites.
the use of chemometrics is a powerful tool for identifying and classifying the different types of contamination and for evaluating the mobility of the contaminants in the soil.
the use of pattern recognition tools is a powerful tool in order to understand the distribution of heavy metals in soils and to identify the areas where the most severe contamination is found.
